page: Amazon Web Services c8gb.24xlarge is a compute-optimized instance built on the Nitro hypervisor and driven by the ARMv9 architecture. The system features 96 dedicated physical cores based on AWS Neoverse-V2 silicon operating at 2.8 GHz, with a single execution thread per core. Memory capacity is allocated at 192.0 GB of RAM, establishing a 2.0 GB per core ratio aligned with compute-intensive design patterns. The instance does not include integrated local SSD storage or discrete GPU hardware, relying instead on network-attached storage architectures and dedicated network throughput rated at 200 Gbps baseline.

Benchmark results demonstrate exceptional multi-core performance, driven by full single-thread-per-core hardware dedication. The instance achieves top-tier results in multi-core metrics, including stress-ng multi-core CPU testing, Geekbench multi-core evaluation, multi-threaded bzip3 decompression, and Clang compilation benchmarks. Cached memory bandwidth delivers up to 11075.0 GB/sec, while uncached large-block reads register at 480.77 GB/sec, which underpins strong PassMark memory and database operation scores. Conversely, single-threaded processing reflects mid-tier performance across single-core Geekbench and stress-ng runs, highlighting an architecture geared primarily for scale-out parallel workloads rather than maximum serial execution.

The 200 Gbps network interface translates into high data throughput, as evidenced by top-tier performance in static web serving and Redis operation benchmarks reaching 194.84 million SET operations per second. CPU-based machine learning inference metrics indicate strong performance for text generation using medium (7B) and large (70B) language models despite lacking dedicated GPU acceleration. Given the lack of local NVMe storage and the low memory-to-core ratio, this server type is best suited for parallel compilation, distributed CI/CD pipelines, high-throughput web frontends, and compute-focused microservice architectures requiring dense parallel scaling.
description: Amazon Web Services c8gb.24xlarge is a compute-optimized cloud instance powered by 96 dedicated ARMv9 Neoverse-V2 physical cores clocked at 2.8 GHz. The server contains 192.0 GB of memory (2.0 GB per core) and delivers a high-speed 200 Gbps baseline network bandwidth. It provides no local instance storage and excludes discrete GPUs, utilizing the Nitro hypervisor architecture. Benchmark testing highlights top-tier multi-threaded processing, software compilation with Clang, ray tracing, and high-throughput memory operations, alongside strong performance in multi-threaded decompression and Redis caching. Single-core performance falls within average ranges, indicating an architecture tailored for concurrent execution. With substantial network capacity and 96 dedicated execution pipelines, this server is well configured for distributed CI/CD pipelines, containerized microservices, scientific simulation, and high-volume web application serving.
